newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief vows to tackle TV liquor ads in July.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief vows to tackle TV liquor ads in July.

text.p: The nation's top communications regulator, forced to scrap plans to investigate liquor advertising on television this month, Monday vowed to reexamine the issue in July.
Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt cited a letter from Attorney General Janet Reno urging him to press forward with an investigation into hard liquor advertisements on television.

In the letter, Reno pointed to the commission's "unique role" in "ensuring that the public interest is not undermined by certain uses of the public airwaves," Hundt said, adding that Reno asked the FCC to report its finding to Congress and the president.
"This should put to rest any suggestion that the Commission lacks juridiction to examine the issues relating to hard liquor's push to get its advertisements on the airwaves," Hundt said.
"I think that the commission has an obligation to gather the facts here, and I do not think that delay is useful," he said.

Hundt's bid to open a probe was derailed when FCC Commissioner Rachelle Chong requested that the item be stricken from the commission's agenda at its June 19 public meeting. Chong had argued that an investigation was outside the agency's jurisdiction and was better handled by the Federal Trade Commission. The FTC is undertaking a probe.
Hundt said he disagreed with Chong's reasoning, but cited the commission's informal tradition of giving a commissioner one strike of any one item one time.
"I think the tradition is a sound one," Hundt said in a statement, adding, "Therefore I will take the notice off the agenda to defer our consideration of the notice to the July meeting."
The liquor industry last year abandoned a decades-old voluntary ban on marketing over the airwavess. President Clinton has called on distillers to discontinue the practice.
